subject.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot

question: Should OpenClaw accept modelExplicit and appliedModel as the ACP runtime-boundary contract for distinguishing inherited Codex ACP defaults from explicit model selections?
rationale: The code appears correct, but this changes fallback versus fail-closed behavior and adds cross-boundary runtime contract fields, which is a compatibility decision automation should not make alone.

options.title: Accept the provenance contract
options.body: Land with modelExplicit and appliedModel because they separate inherited defaults from caller intent and prevent replaying dropped models.

options.title: Document before landing
options.body: Ask for release-note or PR-body wording that explicitly says unsupported explicit Codex ACP model selections fail while inherited non-OpenAI defaults are dropped.

options.title: Request a narrower API
options.body: Pause the branch and ask for a Codex-only contract if generic ACP runtime fields are not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept the provenance contract
recommendation.body: Land with modelExplicit and appliedModel because they separate inherited defaults from caller intent and prevent replaying dropped models.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent owns the most relevant recent ACPX model-runtime history and authored the current blocking review.
